In the NEON branch, advancing array_ptr past the allocation (line 16) and forming array_ptr + array_size (line 13) are pointer-arithmetic validity violations in the oversized/non-divisible cases; dominated by the confirmed OOB write.
INT_MAX-scale sizes could additionally cause index/pointer arithmetic overflow, but are dominated by the confirmed OOB and not separately scored.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown code. All pixel-cache writes through SetPSDPixel stay within the columns-wide row returned by GetAuthenticPixels (loop guards at lines 32, 62, and 70 bound every index to [0, columns-1]). The input-buffer reads at lines 35, 39, and 47 are unbounded in the shown code but their capacity is not identifiable here, so an out-of-bounds read cannot be confirmed; the unchecked GetAuthenticIndexQueue result and unvalidated packet_size are likewise unconfirmable without callee/caller behavior.

assumptions: GetAuthenticPixels at line 27 returns a valid cache region of width image->columns (height 1), so q and the index queue have capacity image->columns, per the standard cache API and the visible width argument.
GetPSDPacketSize returns 1, 2, or 4, consistent with the three branches at lines 34/37/42 and with the channel bytes supplied by the caller.
image->columns and image->depth are positive, parser-validated values; no constraint on them is visible in the shown code.
limitations: Potential out-of-bounds read of the pixels buffer at lines 35, 39, and 47 cannot be confirmed: the shown code reads ceil(columns/8)*packet_size bytes (depth <= 1) or columns*packet_size bytes (depth > 1) with no bounds check, but the buffer capacity is not identifiable from the shown code (no allocation, constant, or length parameter), so the exact excess cannot be demonstrated (CWE-125 unconfirmable).
indexes from GetAuthenticIndexQueue (line 30) is not NULL-checked; a NULL dereference inside SetPSDPixel is not producible on any path visible in the shown code (CWE-476 unconfirmable).

packet_size is not validated before the else branch reads 4 bytes as a float (line 47); a value outside {1,2} from GetPSDPacketSize would mismatch the read size, but the callee's value set is not shown (defensive-hardening concern).
A cast of image->columns (size_t) to ssize_t at line 32 or line 61 could misbehave only if columns > SSIZE_MAX, a parser-side invariant not visible in the shown code.

verdict.summary: In the EXPLICIT-padding branch, explicit_paddings[2..5] are indexed with no size check, so a vector with fewer than 6 elements causes a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Separately, num_groups = in_depth / patch_depth and the lambda divisions dim_size(3) / num_groups are unguarded, so zero-valued or undersized channel dims cause integer division by zero and a process crash (CWE-369).

evidence.reason: CWE-125: explicit_paddings is an entry-point input whose size is never checked in the shown code; the guard at line 63 admits padding == EXPLICIT but imposes no lower bound on the vector size. Its residual size range is 0..n, so an empty vector passes every guard and the read at index 2 dereferences past the heap buffer (capacity 0, required >= 6). The OOB value is then narrowed and passed into SpatialConvolution.
CWE-125: same unguarded indexing as line 67; with explicit_paddings.size() < 4, index 3 reads out of bounds of the heap vector and the result is narrowed to int and passed to SpatialConvolution.
CWE-125: with explicit_paddings.size() < 5 (e.g., the empty vector admitted by the line-63 guard), index 4 is out of bounds; the OOB int64 read is cast to int and passed to SpatialConvolution.

CWE-125: the most severe index of the unguarded sequence; explicit_paddings must hold at least 6 elements for this read to be in-domain, but the shown code never checks size(), so sizes 0..5 pass the EXPLICIT-branch guard and index 5 reads past the heap buffer.

CWE-369: in_depth (line 10) and patch_depth (line 11) are entry-point tensor dims with residual range >= 0 and no check in the shown code; patch_depth == 0 (a filter with zero input channels) makes this integer division by zero, which is UB and crashes the process (SIGFPE). No guard admits or excludes any value here.

CWE-369: num_groups is 0 whenever in_depth == 0 or in_depth < patch_depth (e.g., in_depth 1, patch_depth 2) because num_groups truncates (line 12); when pre_shuffle is first invoked at lines 36-37, this expression divides by zero, crashing the process with no guard in the shown code.

CWE-369: the same unguarded division by num_groups occurs in post_shuffle, which is invoked at lines 35/40/48 before any loop guard; with in_depth == 0 or in_depth < patch_depth the divisor is 0 and the division is UB, crashing the process.

assumptions: Tensor::dim_size returns non-negative int64 values for valid Tensor objects.

The functor can be invoked with framework-supplied tensor shapes and op attributes; the shown code performs no shape or attribute validation, so validation performed in an outer caller is out of scope by the analysis rules.
Eigen/Tensor operations used (shaped, shuffle, chip, tensor assignment) follow their standard semantics.
limitations: The int64_t-to-int narrowing at lines 67-70 demonstrably truncates out-of-range explicit padding values, but whether the truncated values cause memory unsafety inside the unshown SpatialConvolution cannot be confirmed from the shown code.

When in_depth is not divisible by patch_depth, the element-count mismatch makes Tensor::shaped abort the process (lines 37, 42, 81); this is the same availability class as CWE-369 but the CHECK semantics live in the callee, outside the shown code.
The DCHECK on data_format (line 6) is compiled out in release builds, so format validity is not enforced by the shown code; data_format never reaches a sink in the shown code.
Failure of the async Eigen assignments would leave BlockingCounter.Wait() (lines 31-45) or tensor data in an unknown state; no error path is visible in the shown code, so a hang is unconfirmed.
The loop chip indices (lines 59-61) are in-bounds for every i < num_groups because the chipped tensors have dim-0 exactly num_groups, so no OOB chip finding is reported.

verdict.summary: Tensor::FromProto forwards the attacker-controlled tensor_content() bytes and the shape-derived element count N to Helper<T>::Decode (line 12) without any shown check that content.size() equals N * sizeof(T), so an attacker can choose an inconsistent pair (e.g., shape [1] with DT_FLOAT and a 4096-byte content, all members of the guards' admitted sets at lines 4, 5, 8, 10) that a standard byte-decode turns into a heap out-of-bounds write past the N*sizeof(T) buffer; the same unvalidated N is forwarded to FromProtoField (line 15) against the proto's repeated fields.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled content (proto.tensor_content(), residual size >= 1 via the line 10 emptiness guard, no upper bound) and attacker-chosen N (shape.num_elements(), admitted by N > 0 at line 8) are coupled only by their common source proto; the shown code imposes no constraint relating content.size() to N * sizeof(T). Witness: shape [1] gives N = 1; DT_FLOAT is truthy and non-INVALID (lines 5 and 8 admit it); a 4096-byte non-empty tensor_content() is admitted by line 10. A standard byte decode of this (content, N) pairing consumes N as an element count and content as the source bytes, so copying content.size() bytes into an N * sizeof(T) = 4-byte buffer writes 4092 bytes out of bounds (CWE-787 heap OOB write); the reverse pairing (large N, tiny content) is the same missing check manifested as CWE-125. The guard at line 8 is insufficient because it constrains only N > 0 and dtype truthiness, never the content length.

In the tensor_content()-empty branch (line 10's admitted set includes an empty string), the same attacker-chosen N (shape-derived, admitted by N > 0 at line 8 and valid shape at line 4) is forwarded as the element count for populating the tensor from proto's typed repeated value field, without any shown check that the field holds N entries. A standard element-wise decode reads entries 0..N-1, so a shorter attacker-supplied field results in an out-of-bounds read of the same root cause (unvalidated N vs. input size), sharing the CWE-787/125 mechanism of the line 12 sink; reported here as the second distinct sink statement.

assumptions: Helper<T>::Decode is assumed, by its name and call-site use (source bytes from tensor_content, element count N), to allocate storage sized from N and to fill it from content; the exact internal checks are not shown.
FromProtoField is assumed to populate N elements from proto's typed repeated field, consuming N as a length.
TensorShape::IsValid is treated only as whatever gate the (external) implementation provides; its exact bounds are not asserted here.
limitations: The bodies of Helper<T>::Decode and FromProtoField are not shown; if either helper independently validates content.size() == N * sizeof(T) (or field count == N) and rejects mismatches, the overflow is neutralized. This is why confidence is capped at 0.6 despite a fully in-scope witness.

The read-direction manifestation (CWE-125) of the same missing size coupling is not listed as a separate CWE because both directions stem from one unvalidated pairing and only one primary mechanism is confirmed.

An integer-overflow claim on shape.num_elements() (CWE-190) is unconfirmable: TensorShape::IsValid's overflow/dim-count semantics are outside the shown code, and no shown arithmetic computes N * sizeof(T).
A null-allocator abort via CHECK_NOTNULL(a) is a caller-supplied condition, not attacker-reachable within the shown code, and is therefore not a finding.
If TensorShape::IsValid caps the total element count, the maximum exploitable N would shrink accordingly; the shape-validation bound is external to the shown code.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown code. All attacker-derived values are masked to 0..31 (line 14) or 0..3 (line 15), the ue value is range-checked after its cast (lines 128-129), and every memcpy uses the fixed constant sizeof(AVCSliceInfo) (lines 13, 37, 40, 160). The dangerous-looking dereference `n_state.sps->poc_type` (line 80) is guarded for `avc->s_info.sps` (lines 77-78) and, because `n_state` is byte-copied from `avc->s_info` at line 13, a NULL `n_state.sps` can only arise from the unshown callee `avc_parse_slice` (line 54); the discarded `svc_parse_slice` return (line 29) and the `avc_compute_poc` call at line 159 are likewise callee-dependent. Those unconfirmed candidates are recorded in limitations.

assumptions: AVCSliceInfo is a plain value struct containing pointer fields sps and pps; `n_state.sps` and `avc->s_info.sps` are pointers of the same type.
`gf_bs_read_u8` returns 0..255, `gf_bs_read_ue` returns 0..0xFFFFFFFF, and the GF_BitStream reads are internally bounds-safe (framework invariant not shown in this listing).
`n_state.nal_unit_type` can hold 0..31 (assigned from a 5-bit mask) and `AVCState`/`avc->s_info` is initialized by the caller before the first invocation.
The GF_AVC_NALU_* constants used in the switch and comparisons are distinct, so all case labels and the range tests at lines 57-59 and 103-104 are well-defined.
`SVC_ReadNal_header_extension` and `avc_compute_poc` are treated as void-returning; if they return error codes, their results are discarded (lines 27, 34, 44, 159).
limitations: CWE-476 candidate at line 80 (`if (avc->s_info.sps->poc_type == n_state.sps->poc_type)`): the guard at lines 77-78 (`if (!avc->s_info.sps) return -1;`) protects only `avc->s_info.sps`; `n_state.sps` is dereferenced unguarded. Because line 13 copies `avc->s_info` into `n_state`, a NULL `n_state.sps` can only be produced by the unshown callee `avc_parse_slice` (line 54) overwriting it while returning >= 0, so no in-scope witness exists and the NULL-deref confirmation standard is not met.

CWE-703/754 candidate at line 29 (`/*ret = */svc_parse_slice(bs, avc, &n_state);`): the return value is discarded and parsing proceeds to `avc_compute_poc` (line 34) and commits `n_state` to `avc->s_info` (lines 37/40), returning 0/1 as success; whether `svc_parse_slice` returns an error for malformed input is not shown, so the failing step cannot be demonstrated.

CWE-703/754 candidate at lines 54-56: only `ret < 0` is handled; any non-negative error code from `avc_parse_slice` would be overwritten by `ret = 0`. Callee semantics are not shown, so not confirmable.

Reachability note: `if (slice) avc_compute_poc(&n_state);` (lines 158-159) executes with slice==1 on break paths (e.g., line 61) before any SPS guard; if prior state has `avc->s_info.sps == NULL` and the callee leaves `n_state.sps` NULL, `avc_compute_poc` receives a possibly-NULL sps. Whether it dereferences sps is not shown, so this is unconfirmed.

The `GF_AVC_NALU_IDR_SLICE` case (line 47) never sets `idr_flag = 1` (it stays 0 from line 17), so `avc_parse_slice` at line 54 always receives idr_flag==0 for IDR slices; this is a parsing-correctness deviation with no demonstrated memory-safety or injection impact in the shown code.
OOB reads from the bitstream inside `gf_bs_read_*`/`gf_bs_read_ue` would depend on the unshown GF_BitStream implementation, so any such claim is out of scope for this listing.

No attacker-derived index, size, length, format string, file path, command, or query is constructed in the shown code; the only memory operations are fixed-size memcpys, and the only derived storage is `avc->last_ps_idx`, which is range-checked after its cast (lines 128-129) and never used as an index.

verdict.summary: The grouped-convolution kernel divides by attacker-controlled tensor dimensions without any guard: `num_groups = in_depth / patch_depth` (line 12) divides by zero when the filter's depth dimension is 0, and the same unguarded division recurs in `pre_shuffle`/`post_shuffle` (lines 20/26) when `patch_depth > in_depth` makes `num_groups == 0`, crashing the process (CWE-369). Additionally, on the `EXPLICIT` padding path the code indexes `explicit_paddings[2..5]` (lines 76-79) with no size check, causing an out-of-bounds heap read when the vector has fewer than 6 elements (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: patch_depth comes from filter.dim_size(2) (line 11), an entry-point tensor dimension whose residual range is unconstrained [0, 2^63-1] because the shown code never checks it. With patch_depth == 0 (a valid zero-sized filter dimension) the int64 division at line 12 divides by zero, raising SIGFPE and terminating the process. The same unguarded division re-executes at lines 20/26 (via the lambda invocations at lines 37/45/56) whenever patch_depth > in_depth yields num_groups == 0. Primary CWE-369.

explicit_paddings is an internal-helper parameter whose size the shown code never validates, so size() == 0 is in the residual range; the only guard on this path, `padding == EXPLICIT` (line 72), does not constrain the vector size. Index 2 on an empty std::vector is out of the operator[] domain (index < size), producing an OOB heap read. CWE-125.
Same unguarded vector indexing as line 76: with padding == EXPLICIT and explicit_paddings.size() < 4, index 3 is out of the std::vector::operator[] domain, causing an OOB heap read. CWE-125.

Same unguarded vector indexing as line 76: with padding == EXPLICIT and explicit_paddings.size() <= 4 (e.g., size 0), index 4 is out of the std::vector::operator[] domain, causing an OOB heap read. CWE-125.

Same unguarded vector indexing as line 76: with padding == EXPLICIT and explicit_paddings.size() <= 5 (e.g., size 0), index 5 is out of the std::vector::operator[] domain, causing an OOB heap read. CWE-125.

assumptions: input, filter, and output tensors have rank >= 4 and are non-null; this is enforced by the framework op, not by the shown code.
TensorFlow tensor dimensions may legitimately be 0, so patch_depth == 0 is a representable, permitted value in the shown code's domain.
explicit_paddings is supplied by an out-of-scope caller; the shown code itself imposes no size constraint, so sizes < 6 are analyzed as admitted values.
limitations: dim_size(3)/dim_size(2) on tensors with rank < 4 is not guarded here (release-mode DCHECK-only); callers are expected to validate rank.
The int64_t -> int narrowing casts at lines 76-79 (CWE-681) are unconfirmed: the security impact of wrapped padding values depends on the unshown SpatialConvolution callee.
row_stride/col_stride/row_dilation/col_dilation are forwarded unvalidated (lines 73-75, 81-83); validation, if any, lives outside the shown code.

A non-divisible in_depth/patch_depth combination (e.g., in_depth=7, patch_depth=3) aborts inside Tensor::shaped at line 40 (element-count CHECK); it is a crash of the same missing-validation root family as the division-by-zero finding, not a separate CWE.
shuffles_completed.Wait() (line 51) could hang if Eigen's async assignment never invokes the done callback for empty tensors; Eigen internals are not shown, so this is unconfirmed.
The DCHECK data_format assertion (lines 6-8) is compiled out in release builds; passing non-NHWC would yield wrong results but no memory-safety violation here.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown code. The only writable objects with identifiable capacity are the pixel/index regions acquired by GetAuthenticPixels(image,0,row,image->columns,1,...) at line 27, and both the depth>1 path (line 52) and the depth==1 bit-unpacking path (lines 61-70) write exactly image->columns times (indices 0..columns-1), so no out-of-bounds write has a reachable witness. The unbounded reads from the pixels buffer (lines 35, 39, 47) are a genuine concern, but the buffer's capacity is not identifiable from the shown code, so the over-read cannot be confirmed per the capacity rule and is recorded as a limitation.

assumptions: GetPSDPacketSize returns only 1, 2, or 4, matching the three branches of the packet_size dispatch (depth<=8/<=16/else).
GetAuthenticPixels returns a 1-row region with exactly image->columns pixel slots and a matching index queue when one exists.
The caller that supplies pixels is responsible for its length; no length validation exists inside this function.
limitations: Heap/stack buffer over-read of pixels (potential CWE-125): the function consumes columns*packet_size bytes (1/2/4 per iteration at lines 35, 39, 47) without any length parameter or allocation in view, so a caller passing a shorter buffer would cause an over-read; the capacity of pixels is not identifiable from the shown code and the guard lives in unshown caller code, so the claim is unconfirmable here.

NULL dereference of indexes inside SetPSDPixel is unconfirmed: GetAuthenticIndexQueue at line 30 can return NULL only based on image cache state set outside the shown code, and the dereference is inside the unshown callee.

Resource exhaustion via a huge attacker-controlled image->columns is not confirmable: the loop is bounded by columns, but the enormous GetAuthenticPixels allocation at line 27 would have to succeed first, and its failure is handled by the NULL check at lines 28-29.
If image->columns exceeds SSIZE_MAX, the cast at line 32 is implementation-defined and the loop is skipped; this produces no sink value and is treated as a robustness note only.

verdict.summary: The attacker-controlled PixMap 'pixelsize' field (u16 read at pos+18, residual range 0..65535 with no constraint) is used as the divisor at line 32 without any non-zero check, so a crafted file with 0x0000 in that field (or an out-of-range read returning 0) triggers an integer divide-by-zero (SIGFPE), crashing the parser with a DoS.

evidence.reason: Division sink: bi->pixelsize is filled from dbuf_getu16be(f, pos+18) (line 26), an unconstrained entry-point file read whose admitted range includes 0. No check excludes 0 before this statement; the only conditional (lines 33-35) runs after the division and compares pdwidth to npwidth, so it cannot protect the divisor. Witness: pixelsize=0 (file bytes 0x0000 at pos+18) with any rowbytes value reaches the sink on every call and faults with integer division by zero (CWE-369).

assumptions: Standard C semantics apply: integer division by zero is undefined behavior and traps (SIGFPE) on common platforms.
dbuf_getu16be returns the file value as data; no constraint in the shown code prevents the value 0.
bi->rowbytes and bi->npwidth are set outside this snippet; their ranges are unknown from the shown code but are not needed for the confirmed finding.
limitations: Out-of-range dbuf reads at pos+0 .. pos+32 cannot be confirmed as OOB: the capacity of f and the out-of-range behavior of dbuf_getu16be/u32be/pict_read_fixed are not visible in the shown code (no identified capacity, no boundary claim).
Overflow of (bi->rowbytes*8) in i64 cannot be confirmed: rowbytes' range and provenance are not shown, and no consuming sink is in this snippet; it is not reported as CWE-190.
A very small positive pixelsize (e.g., 1) could make pdwidth huge and affect later allocations, but the consuming code is outside the shown snippet, so this is unconfirmable.
The (int)/(unsigned int) narrowing casts in de_dbg calls can corrupt only debug output and have no security impact.
i64 wrap in pos+32 as a theoretical read-offset issue is unconfirmable and would be neutralized by the dbuf layer's semantics, which are not shown.

verdict.summary: diST_box_read reads box bytes into a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer str without bounding the index i, so a crafted file whose payload begins with 1024 or more consecutive non-zero bytes triggers an out-of-bounds stack write (str[1024] and beyond), enabling memory corruption from a malicious media file.

evidence.reason: Entry-point bytes from gf_bs_read_u8 (residual range 1..255 for each non-terminating iteration) drive i via the line 12 increment, with no upper-bound check against the 1024-byte capacity declared at line 4 (valid indices 0..1023). The only guard, `if (!str[i]) break;` (line 11), admits every non-zero byte and is evaluated after the write, so it cannot bound i for the next iteration. Witness: payload of 1024 consecutive 0x41 bytes makes i reach 1024, and this sink writes str[1024] — index equal to capacity, out of bounds by at least 1 byte (more for longer non-zero runs) — a stack OOB write (CWE-787).

assumptions: gf_bs_read_u8 returns a byte in 0..255 and returns 0 at EOF/error; this terminates the loop at stream end but does not prevent the overflow, which triggers on in-stream non-zero bytes.
ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE is the standard GPAC macro that errors when p->size is smaller than the given count; even so, it is invoked only after the read loop has already run.
limitations: Reads past the box's declared remaining size occur before ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(p, i) at line 14 validates the count; the check is applied after consumption, so it cannot prevent the overflow (dominated by the CWE-787 finding, no separate CWE).

Unchecked gf_strdup result at line 16 could be NULL on allocation failure, but the shown code never dereferences it; allocation-failure DoS without attacker control of the allocation is not a confirmed finding.
A u32 wrap of i would require a ~4 GiB non-zero run, which is preempted by the earlier out-of-bounds write; not reported.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown code: every memory operation is a fixed-size AVCSliceInfo memcpy with no attacker-derived index or size, and each candidate (assert-guarded sps dereference at line 79, discarded svc_parse_slice status at line 29, constant idr_flag at line 54, gf_bs_read_ue cast at line 127) fails the reachability/impact confirmation standard because the required NULL or failure values are produced only by callee behavior or caller state not visible in the shown code.

assumptions: avc->s_info is an AVCSliceInfo member of AVCState, consistent with the fixed-size memcpy uses at lines 13, 37, 40, 159.
gf_bs_read_u8 returns u8 (0..255) and gf_bs_read_ue returns u32 (0..2^32-1), per their use in the shown code.
assert has standard C semantics and is compiled out under NDEBUG (release builds).
avc_parse_slice signals failure with a negative return, as the shown code checks at line 55.
limitations: NULL dereference of avc->s_info.sps / n_state.sps at line 79 (and the poc_type reads at lines 80/90) is unconfirmed: producing a NULL sps on that path requires avc_parse_slice (line 54) to leave n_state.sps NULL, an earlier call to leave avc->s_info.sps NULL, or caller-supplied avc state — none visible in the shown code. The only in-scope guard, assert(avc->s_info.sps) at line 77, is compiled out in release builds and does not cover n_state.sps; this is the most probable latent CWE-476 if the callee can leave sps NULL.

Discarded return of svc_parse_slice at line 29: if the helper signals failure, lines 34-41 compute POC and return 1/0 as success, but the helper's failure convention and any downstream impact are not visible in the shown code (error-handling robustness, no CWE).

idr_flag is constant 0 (line 17) and is passed for IDR slices at line 54; if the callee depends on it to parse idr_pic_id/POC, IDR slices may be mis-parsed, but the callee is not shown and no memory/injection sink in the shown code is affected.

gf_bs_read_ue at line 127 can return up to 2^32-1; the negative s32 wrap is caught at line 128, but positive values up to 2^31-1 stored in last_ps_idx are used as an index only outside the shown code, so any resulting out-of-bounds access is unconfirmable here.
EOF at gf_bs_read_u8 (line 10) is indistinguishable from a genuine zero byte and only affects AU-boundary heuristics; no memory impact is visible in the shown code.
The shown code contains no loop constructs, so no iteration-bound or sentinel-overrun analysis applies within it.

verdict.summary: No confirmed exploitable vulnerability in the shown code. The PCL byte-scan loop filling command[MagickPathExtent] is bounded by the guard at lines 116-118: the reset (with its NUL write) is forced as soon as (p-command) reaches MagickPathExtent-1, so the maximum content byte is at index MagickPathExtent-2 and the NUL at MagickPathExtent-1, both within the declared capacity. The only values that reach the delegate shell command are numeric (%g/%.20g) strings and library-generated unique filenames, so no injection is demonstrable from the shown code; the remaining concerns (stale count reuse, float-to-size_t conversion UB, ThrowReaderException internals, unique-filename metacharacter survival) have no sink in the shown code and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: MagickPathExtent is the compile-time capacity of the local buffers declared at lines 9-14 (command, filename, geometry, input_filename).
ReadBlobByte() returns byte values 0..255 or EOF, and the for-loop condition at line 108 excludes EOF from the loop body, so the body runs only for 0..255.
SegmentInfo fields x1/y1/x2/y2 are double, matching the %lf conversions in sscanf at lines 131-146.

AcquireString() (lines 186-187) allocates at least MagickPathExtent bytes per its standard semantics, so the FormatLocaleString calls with size MagickPathExtent at lines 188, 194, 202 and 205 stay in bounds.
limitations: If the loop-bound test at line 117 were (p-command) < MagickPathExtent (without -1), the NUL at line 119 would be written one past the end; the shown code uses MagickPathExtent-1 and is safe, so no CWE is confirmed.

count is not reset per parsed line (initialized once at line 102); after a successful CropBox/MediaBox parse a non-matching line reuses stale bounds at lines 153-158, but only re-applies previously validated numeric values with no memory or command impact.

Attacker-chosen coordinates (e.g., x2 < x1 or values near 1e308, lines 153-154) can make floor() negative or infinite; casting to size_t is undefined behavior, but the result is only formatted numerically (lines 168-169, 194-195) and never used as an index/size/length/pointer in the shown code.

Whether shell metacharacters in image_info->filename survive AcquireUniqueSymbolicLink/AcquireUniqueFilename (lines 70, 213) into the delegate command executed at line 221 cannot be verified: those transformations are not shown, so command injection is unconfirmed.
The expansion of ThrowReaderException at line 228 is not shown; whether it dereferences image while image is NULL cannot be verified from the shown code.

The scan loop (lines 108-159) reads the whole file byte-by-byte even when image_info->page is set (lines 110-111); this is linear work with no attacker-controlled amplification and is not a resource-exhaustion finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only dangerous-looking operation, the division at line 33, is fully protected by the line 32 guard whose admitted set is pixelsize in 1..65535 (0 excluded). The unchecked-pos reads, rowbytes*8 overflow, discarded dbuf return values, and int-narrowing casts all fail three-part confirmation: buffer capacity, field provenance, and callee bounds semantics are not identifiable in the shown code, so no concrete out-of-domain witness or reachable impact can be anchored.

assumptions: Callers are expected to pass a `pos` and a `dbuf *f` such that the 36 bytes at `pos` (lines 12-45) lie within `f`; no such invariant is visible in the shown code.
`bi->rowbytes` and `bi->npwidth` are populated before this function runs; their provenance and magnitudes are not visible in the shown code.
`dbuf_getu16be`/`dbuf_getu32be`/`pict_read_fixed` fail/behave in some unspecified way on out-of-range offsets; their bodies are not shown.
limitations: OOB read via unchecked `pos`: every read offset (pos+0 ... pos+32, lines 12, 15, 18, 21, 22, 25-28, 39, 42, 45) is derived from the unconstrained i64 parameter `pos` with no bounds check in the shown code. A confirmed witness cannot be produced because `f`'s capacity and the accessors' bounds behavior are not identifiable from the shown code; if those accessors do not bounds-check, an attacker-influenced `pos` could read past the buffer.

Integer overflow (CWE-190): `bi->rowbytes*8` at line 33 can wrap i64 only for `rowbytes` exceeding ~2^60-1, a magnitude the shown code cannot establish; the product also reaches no allocation-size, index, or length sink in the shown code.

Error/status handling: none of the dbuf read statuses are checked; `pack_size` (line 18) and `plane_bytes` (line 39) are consumed only by debug logging, so any 'proceed after failed read' behavior and its impact depend on callee behavior not shown.

Narrowing casts to `int` (lines 9, 13, 19, 30, 40, 43, 46) can truncate large i64 values, but the truncated results reach only literal-format numeric debug output; no injection or memory-safety impact is confirmed.

verdict.summary: The u32 config-size counter is decremented by 4 at line 40 with no size>=4 check; for an attacker-supplied size of 1..3 bytes it wraps to ~UINT32_MAX, defeating the OBU loop bound (line 42) and the size<obu_size guard (line 72). Attacker-controlled OBU size fields then reach the allocation sink at line 61 and the read sink at line 67 with no effective config-length cap, enabling oversized allocations/reads beyond the declared AV1 config (bounds bypass / resource exhaustion).

evidence.reason: Entry-point u32 parameter `size` has residual range 1..2^32-1 (the only shown constraint is `if (!size) return NULL` at line 9); a value of 2 makes line 40 wrap to 0xFFFFFFFE in u32 arithmetic. The while-loop condition at line 42 and the guard `if (size<obu_size)` at line 72 (which executes only after the allocation/read at lines 61/67) then admit obu_size values up to ~UINT32_MAX, so attacker-set OBU size fields drive `gf_malloc((size_t)obu_size)` and `gf_bs_read_data(..., (u32)obu_size)` far beyond the real remaining config bytes. Root cause is the unsigned underflow of the length/budget counter (CWE-191); the missing protections are a `size >= 4` check before line 40 and an `obu_size > size` check before line 61.

assumptions: The caller supplies `size` as the byte length of the av1C config payload, i.e., an attacker can choose values 1..3 for a truncated box.
`gf_bs_*` calls operate over an attacker-controlled bitstream and clamp reads at the underlying stream end, so reads past the config boundary stay within the file buffer.
`gf_av1_parse_obu` derives `obu_size` from the OBU header fields present in the attacker-controlled bytes.
limitations: A direct out-of-bounds write is not derivable: `gf_malloc((size_t)obu_size)` (line 61) and `gf_bs_read_data(..., (u32)obu_size)` (line 67) truncate identically on 32-bit builds and allocation >= read on 64-bit builds.

Whether `gf_av1_parse_obu` actually returns near-4GiB `obu_size` values, and whether `gf_bs_read_data` clamps a short read, depend on unshown callee bodies; the memory-exhaustion impact assumes the parser accepts large size fields.

The discarded return of `gf_bs_read_data` (line 67) combined with `a->obu_length = obu_size` (line 68) can overstate initialized bytes if the stream ends early; that hazard materializes only in out-of-scope consumers of `cfg->obu_array`.
An unchecked NULL from `gf_odf_av1_cfg_new()` (line 11) dereferenced at line 15 would require an uncontrolled fixed-size allocation failure and is not attacker-controlled.
Non-termination of `while (size)` (line 42) would require `gf_av1_parse_obu` to return GF_OK without consuming bytes; unboundedness is not confirmable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: All tensor accesses and the batch-ordering loop in MakeDataset are provably in-bounds: the row index is bounded by `i < indices->dim_size(0)` (line 43) and column 0 exists because `dense_shape->NumElements() > 0` with `dense_shape` length equal to `indices` columns (lines 27, 32). Every status-returning call is checked via OP_REQUIRES_OK. The only residual gaps — batch indices may be negative (the ordering guard admits values >= -1 via previous_batch_index = -1) and dense_shape element values are unvalidated — flow solely into unshown callees (SparseTensor::Create, Dataset<T>), so no failure is confirmable within the shown code.

assumptions: Tensor shape dims (dim_size) are non-negative and finite because `indices`/`values`/`dense_shape` are existing Tensor objects fetched from the framework (lines 5, 7, 9); this makes the loop bound N finite and the column count D >= 1 given lines 27 and 32.

The op registration or upstream SparseTensor producer fixes the dtypes of `indices`/`dense_shape` so that `matrix<int64_t>()`/`vec<int64_t>()` (lines 44, 56) reinterpret stored int64 data; no dtype check is visible in the shown code.
limitations: Batch indices are only checked for non-decreasing order against `previous_batch_index = -1` (lines 42-50), so any value >= -1, including -1 and values above the dense batch dimension, is admitted. A negative batch index would only cause an out-of-bounds row read inside the unshown `SparseTensor::Create`/`Dataset<T>` slicing logic (lines 54-58); the shown code never passes this value as an index/size/length argument to a call, so the OOB (potential CWE-125) is not confirmable here — it depends on unshown callee behavior.

`dense_shape` element values receive no range check in the shown code (only length checks at lines 27 and 32); negative or inconsistent dims flow into `TensorShape(dense_shape->vec<int64_t>())` and `SparseTensor::Create` (line 56). Any fault (invalid-shape invariant, crash, downstream mis-slicing) occurs in unshown code and is unconfirmed.

No dtype validation precedes `indices->matrix<int64_t>()` (line 44) or `dense_shape->vec<int64_t>()` (line 56); a dtype mismatch would be a misinterpretation/crash only under a framework invariant violation that cannot be established from the shown code.
